newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks steady in overall bearish trend.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks steady in overall bearish trend.

text.p: Jordanian stocks were steady at start of weekly trade on Saturday but Middle East tension continued to cast its shadow and paralyse activity on the politically-sensitive bourse, brokers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose a slight 0.03 percent to 147.63 points from 147.59 on Wednesday.

Market leader Arab Bank, which propelled the index upwards in the first half of September, lacked impetus. Its stock, the most expensive on the Amman exchange, rose 0.500 dinars to 242.500 in very thin trade.
A total of 231,266 shares changed hands in thin 229,574 dinar volume. Sixteen stocks shed gains against 12 advancing and eight unchanged.

Brokers said market activity was dormant with minimal trade with few interested buyers. Most investors, both floor traders and institutional players, were waiting on the sidelines until a clearer picture emerged on Palestinian-Israeli talks after the recent flareup of violence.
After gradual gains that sent the market back above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares began to weaken after clashes flared in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

The market, one of the most politically sensitive in the region, was hit this year by the breakdown of Middle East peace talks and the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner, Iraq.
Banks led the market on Saturday with Middle East Investment Bank dominating activity, followed by weak trade in industrials and services.
